summary: The candidate is mathematically correct under its stated global-extension hypothesis. The parity reindexing, nonnegative decomposition, conditional-midpoint bounds, and finite-second-moment equality argument are valid, including zero weights and zero gain. Tensorization gives the stated equivalences and amplification constants. The maximum-slice inequalities, primitive-lattice reduction, and pointwise depth transfers preserve the required dimensions, fiber volumes, and order of quantifiers. The accepted one-dimensional stability theorem and even-thinning theorem are applied with matching hypotheses and normalizations. The Cauchy convolution identity, exceptional central term, conditioning estimate, truncation bounds, and explicit failure of log-concavity all check exactly. The cited DLMF expansions at https://dlmf.nist.gov/4.36 and the centroid inequality on pages 1259-1260 of https://msp.org/pjm/1960/10-4/pjm-v10-n4-p18-s.pdf were checked and have the stated applicability. No mathematical errors or gaps were found.
